mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day period with similar FEDFUNDS path (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% in a month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive relative to a 5-day moving average baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the housing market shows sustained monthly increases in new residential construction (HOUST) exceeding 5% while inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 3%, it indicates a resilient demand environment that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% in a month and CPIAUCSL < 3 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward log-returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests supply-side pressures that reduce growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in a month and CPIAUCSL decreases by > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, the discount rate is effectively lowered, enhancing the present value of equities and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 60-day prior period with similar FEDFUNDS path (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in layoffs (implied via UNRATE stability) indicates a tight labor market that boosts corporate hiring and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 20% in a month while UNRATE remains flat for two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: During a sharp decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% accompanied by a sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 8%, supply constraints reduce growth expectations and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% and INDPRO falls by > 8% in a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the event.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in retail sales proxy (implied via HOUST or PAYEMS) coupled with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% creates optimism about future demand, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 3% for two months and UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) despite the signal.
